summary: Independent re-verification of the P3a follow-up (subtle 240ms fade-in on the 'ORA remembers this' chip). Ran the updated p3 suite (13/13 pass, including the 3 new fade-in tests) plus full regression sweep across p2 audit spine, ci leak linter, plain-english contract, p1 egress net, show-outcome-not-engine, and ship e2e real push (36 passed + 1 expected SKIP for app_installation_missing on ship_e2e_real_push). CSS additive change verified in /app/frontend/src/index.css (lines 1249-1263): new @keyframes aurem-remembers-fade-in (opacity + 3px translateY, 240ms ease-out both) and matching prefers-reduced-motion override. ChatPanel.jsx line 4687-4688 confirmed to have className='aurem-remembers-chip' added to the ora-remembers-chip div. Frontend smoke test on the public Preview URL: homepage loads cleanly (hero, nav, promo banner, pricing signals all render, no console/DOM errors), and runtime check confirms .aurem-remembers-chip / @keyframes aurem-remembers-fade-in are present in the compiled stylesheet. Did NOT re-trigger Quiet Leak Digest send (per instructions). Did NOT attempt live in-app chat UI screenshot of the fade-in — same pre-existing env gap (test_admin_001 lacks a working GitHub App install; project-scoped chat returns empty) that was already documented in prior passes; this is an environment gap, not a bug in this change.
critical_code_review_comments: CSS change is minimal, additive-only, follows the exact same pattern as the neighboring .aurem-countdown-urgent block (same reduced-motion override style) — good consistency.
Animation duration 240ms + ease-out is genuinely subtle (not flashy), non-looping (both keyword freezes final state), and correctly respects prefers-reduced-motion. Matches P3a intent.
className on the chip is additive; existing inline style + gating logic (m.plainEnglishContractActive && councilRecalled>0) preserved as required.
test_credentials: N/A this pass — no auth flow exercised; homepage smoke only.
context_for_next_testing_agent: P3a fade-in change is fully green. If a future pass wants to visually confirm the fade-in in the running app, the env blocker is: test_admin_001 has no GitHub App installation, and the UI forces a project scope on chat, so project-scoped chat calls return empty content and the 'ORA remembers this' chip never renders in the live UI. This is orthogonal to the fade-in change. Fix the GitHub App install for test_admin_001 (or add a non-project-scoped chat path) before attempting a live screenshot. All backend unit-level assertions for the fade-in already cover: class presence, reduced-motion override presence, duration in 150-400ms window, and non-looping.
